result:
I have the full path now. Here's how a typed `@handle` becomes a sitting notification.

**1. Typing, client side.** `MentionTextarea` (`src/components/domain/comment/mention-textarea.tsx`) drives the `@` autocomplete as the user types, and `CommentComposer` (`src/components/domain/comment/comment-composer.tsx:29`) tracks the ids the UI resolved (`mentioned`) and submits them alongside the raw body as `mentionedUserIds` in the create-comment payload. This client list is only a hint — the server re-derives the truth from the text.

**2. Action boundary.** `createCommentAction` (`src/actions/comments/create-comment.ts`) validates the payload against `createCommentSchema`, checks `can(actor, "comment:create", …)`, consumes the `comment:create` rate-limit bucket, and calls `createComment` in the comment service. It does not touch mentions or notifications itself.

**3. Handle → real user.** `createComment` (`src/server/services/comment-service.ts:45`) calls its own `resolveMentionedUsers(orgId, body, input.mentionedUserIds)` (`comment-service.ts:174`). That function loads up to `MENTION_LOOKUP_LIMIT` (100) org members via `memberRepo.listMembers`, then calls `resolveMentions(body, members)` from `src/lib/mentions.ts:45`. `resolveMentions` runs `extractMentions()` (`mentions.ts:26`), which applies `MENTION_PATTERN` (`mentions.ts:14`, `@` must follow line-start/whitespace/punctuation, never mid-email) after stripping fenced/inline code via `withoutCode()`, so mentions inside code blocks don't count. Each surviving handle is matched against `handleOf(member)` (`mentions.ts:21`) — the lowercased local part of the member's email — to get a `UserId`. Unknown handles (typos, non-members) are silently dropped; the comment write never fails because of a bad mention. `resolveMentionedUsers` then unions this server-resolved set with whatever client-provided ids are still verifiably org members, server list winning on disagreement.

**4. Persistence and event.** The comment is inserted via `commentRepo.insertComment` with the final `mentionedUserIds` attached, then `createComment` calls `emit("comment.created", { …, mentionedUserIds })` (`comment-service.ts:77`, using `emit` from `src/lib/event-bus.ts:54`). This is the list that "carries forward" — everything downstream reads this array rather than re-parsing the markdown.

**5. Fan-out subscription.** `notification-service.ts` attaches its bus subscribers at module load (`registerFanOut()`, `notification-service.ts:180`), reached because `event-registry.ts` imports the module (`import "./notification-service"`, `event-registry.ts:21`), and `registerEventHandlers()` runs once at process start from `instrumentation.ts`. The `"comment.created"` handler (`notification-service.ts:203`) first notifies issue watchers as `comment_created`, then — only if `mentionedUserIds.length > 0` — calls `notify(orgId, "comment_mention", mentionedUserIds, {...})` (`notification-service.ts:216`).

**6. Per-recipient channel decision.** `notify()` (`notification-service.ts:46`) is the actual fan-out hub. For each unique recipient it skips the case where the recipient is the comment's own author (self-mentions produce nothing), then loads that user's `NotificationPreference` for the `comment_mention` kind via `preferenceRepo.getPreference` (`notification-preference-repository.ts:36`; `null` means no explicit row was ever saved). `resolveChannels(preference, flags)` (`notification-service.ts:156`) turns that into a channel list: no preference row → `DEFAULT_CHANNELS = ["in_app", "email"]`; otherwise `in_app` is included iff `preference.inApp`, and `email` is included iff `preference.email` is true **and** either `!preference.digestOnly` or the org's `digest_email` feature flag is enabled (`isEnabled()` from `src/lib/feature-flags.ts`). If both come out false, the recipient is skipped entirely — no row of any kind. Otherwise a row (recipientId, kind, title/body/href, actorId, channels) is queued and all queued rows are bulk-written by `notificationRepo.insertNotifications` (`notification-repository.ts:91`) — this insert is what actually puts the "You were mentioned" row in the recipient's in-app inbox.

**7. What "email" in `channels` actually means.** Storing `"email"` on the row does *not* trigger an immediate email — there's no instant mailer for `comment_mention`. The only place a notification actually turns into a sent email is the daily `runDigestEmailJob` (`src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts`), scheduled per org at `org.settings.digestHourUtc`. It calls `listDigestRecipients` → `preferenceRepo.listDigestSubscribers` (`notification-preference-repository.ts:87`), i.e. only users with `digestOnly = true` on at least one preference kind, then `digest-service.ts`'s `buildDigest()` pulls **all** of that user's unread notifications since the last window via `notificationRepo.listUnreadSince` (not filtered by channel), renders them, and sends one batched email through `sendEmail` (`email-service.ts`), afterward marking those notifications read so the next tick doesn't resend them.

So the end state for a given `@mention` is one of: nothing (handle didn't match a member, or the mentioned user was the commenter, or both channels resolved empty); an in-app row only; an in-app row plus that mention rolled into the recipient's next daily digest email if they're a `digestOnly` subscriber (or the plan's `digest_email` flag gates it off, dropping back to in-app only even if `preference.email` is set).
